''16, 31''.}}∷ by faith purifying their hartes. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}} Novv therfore vvhy tempt you God, to put a yoke vpon the neckes of the di{{ls}}ciples, vvhich neither our fathers nor vve haue been able to beare? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}} but by the grace of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} vve beleeue to be {{ls}}aued, in like maner as they al{{ls}}o.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}} And al the multitude held their peace: and they heard Barnabas and Paul telling vvhat great {{ls}}ignes and vvonders God had done among the Gentiles by them.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}} And after they held their peace, {{sup|‖}} Iames an{{ls}}wered, {{ls}}aying, Men brethren, heare me. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}} Simon hath told hovv God fir{{ls}}t vi{{ls}}ited to take of the Gentiles a people to his name. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}} And to this accord the vvordes of the prophets, as it is vvritten: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Tim. 3, 5.''}}* ''After the{{ls}}e things I vvil returne, and vvil reedifie the tabernacle of Dauid, which was fallen, and the ruines thereof I vvil reedifie, and {{ls}}et it vp'': {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}} ''that the re{{ls}}idue of men may {{ls}}eeke after the Lord, and al nations vpon whom my name is inuocated, {{ls}}aith the Lord that doeth the{{ls}}e things''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}} To our Lord vvas his ovvne vvorke knovven from the beginning of the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}} For the vvhich cau{{ls}}e I iudge, that they vvhich of the Gentiles are conuerted to God, are not to be di{{ls}}quieted, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}} but to write vnto them that they refraine them {{ls}}elues from the contaminations of Idols, and fornication, and {{ls}}trangled things, and bloud. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}} For Moy{{ls}}es of old times hath in euery citie them that preach him in the {{ls}}ynagogs, vvhere he is read euery Sabboth.<noinclude>{{rh|||Then}}</noinclude>
